outcome: hospital performance in achieving spontaneous vaginal birth (SVB) rate targets for Black women at low risk for caesarean birth
SVB rate equivalence between Black and White women at low risk for caesarean birth
cohort: The study sample included 257 hospitals across four states, which were categorized as high-performing or low-performing based on their spontaneous vaginal birth rates for Black women and equity metrics.
finding: High-performing hospitals, characterized by better spontaneous vaginal birth rates and equity for Black women, exhibited better nurse work environments (including nurse-physician relationships) and had more advanced practice nurses on their maternity units.
mod_finding: Better rated nurse work environments and the presence of advanced practice nurses were distinguishing characteristics of high-performing hospitals regarding their spontaneous vaginal birth rates for Black women and SVB rate equivalence between Black and White patients.
